we took a review of the accessible parking permit program for the city's on street pay parking zones. The review evaluated program provisions and current on street accessible parking infrastructure within pay parking areas. The intent of the review is largely to ensure that the program meets stakeholder needs and is consistent with best practices. The city's accessible parking permit program operates in tandem with the Sask build is placard program and takes the form of a sticker fixed to the Sask build a placard.
The parking permit provides free parking for permanent holders and allows users to park beyond the post to time limits in pay parking stalls for up to 72 hours.
A review of on street accessible parking infrastructure identified a count of 10 accessible parking spaces in 157 on street loading zones within the pay parking areas.
With it being noted that placard and permanent holders are also able to utilize loading zone spaces for up to the post to time limit on the street.
The review identified variants in the frequency and size of accessible parking spaces and in the proximity of accessible parking spaces to nearby curb cuts.
Engagement with industry stakeholders was undertaken through two phases to solicit general feedback on the program and then to obtain feedback on any proposed program changes.
Key themes expressed during engagement related to an inadequate number of on street accessible parking stalls, a lack of awareness about the program.
A desire to continue the program in some way and a desire for online improvements to automate the purchasing process.
In response to the stakeholder feedback and review recommended changes include developing on street accessible parking standards that are applied on a consistent basis.
Ensuring a certain size and frequency of accessible parking spaces, consistent standards for demarcation and proximity to curb cuts.
This work would be carried out by community standards and transportation, drawing upon the accessible loading zone pilot project currently underway by transportation.
Increasing program fees from $20 to $100. These have not increased for this program since 1991.
An increase is needed to support cost recovery efforts associated with administering the program and to align with best practices.
It's noted that the proposed increase would be phased in over a two-year period with a $60 fee in $20, $24 and $100 fee in 2025.
A subsidized permit at half the cost would also be offered for those that qualify based on income levels.
Reducing the allowable time restrictions for permanent holders from 72 hours to four hours.
The still exceeds posted time limits within pay parking areas and facilities a reasonable degree of parking turnover with the four hour time allowance being comparable to what other cities offer.
Developing a streamlined automated permit purchasing process, which is a component of a parking technology project.
This report includes two recommendations and I'd be pleased to take any questions.
